findings.finding: Vinmonopolet's own through-September file shows Norwegian monopoly volumes worsening in Q3 2026: Q3 wine (svakvin) -5.8% and spirits (brennevin) -4.0% y/y (derived from the Jan-Sep and H1 sheets), against -2.5% / -2.6% in H1. That is worse than the 2-3% monopoly decline Inderes assumed for Q3, and it hits Anora's Wine segment (market leader in Norway) and Norwegian spirits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26, a volume-led miss (Inderes: 'volyymilasku painoi tuloksen alle odotusten'), -6.8% on 2026-05-06. Q2'26 sales beat on Industrial, +10.3% on 2026-08-14 (with the Bacardi LOI the same morning)
findings.original_quote: Ved utgangen av september er salget ned 3,2 prosent målt mot samme periode i fjor. Det er nedgang for vin og brennevin, men vekst for øl og alkoholfritt. (By end-September sales are down 3.2% on the same period last year; wine and spirits down, beer and alcohol-free up.) Page https://www.vinmonopolet.no/om-oss/salgstall/2026, 'Sist oppdatert: 21. oktober 2026'
findings.why_not_priced: Inderes's preview of 28 Oct still describes monopoly volume declines as 'pitkälti alkuvuoden tapaisena (2-3 % lasku)' (much like early in the year), and the Q3 split has to be derived from two Norwegian spreadsheets. Had the market priced it, the consensus Q3 EBITDA would sit below Inderes's, not 1m above it. Wine EBITDA is small (0.9m in Q2), so the money is modest: net of the rest of the company, about EUR 1m of sales and 0.3-0.5m of EBITDA.
